source.title: Teleological reasoning in infancy: the naive theory of rational action

confidence_rationale: Authoritative synthesis of the converging one-year-old goal-attribution literature into a single inferential principle (the teleological stance / principle of rational action). It supplies MECH-129 with the inference rule by which a goal is attributed and an action evaluated as serving or not serving it -- the bridge between discriminant (1) what the goal is and discriminant (2) whether an action obstructs it. Confidence held below 0.7 because it is a theoretical review (not a single experiment) and because the teleological stance is explicitly NON-mentalistic, which both helps and limits the mapping to MECH-129's consent/constitutive discriminants.
failure_signatures: The teleological stance is explicitly non-mentalistic: it relates action, goal-state, and situational constraints via efficiency, WITHOUT attributing beliefs or commitments. So it grounds MECH-129 discriminants (1)+(2) but NOT (4) consent, which requires the other's commitment/mental state -- exactly the gap the plan assigns to RHM-3 / mirror_modelling_other_self_v5.

Efficiency-based goal attribution can misfire when an agent's behaviour is inefficient for good reason (constraint the observer cannot see); a REE goal-interference signal built on the rationality principle inherits this misattribution risk.

mapping.source_claim_statement: One-year-olds interpret others' goal-directed actions using a non-mentalistic 'teleological stance' -- relating action, goal-state, and situational constraints through a principle of rational action (agents pursue goals by the most efficient means available). This inferential principle is continuous with the later mentalistic rationality principle.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-129's goal-interference signal needs not just the other's goal represented (Woodward) but an inference rule that says whether a given trajectory serves or defeats that goal. The principle of rational action is that rule: given an inferred goal and the situational constraints, an efficient path is expected, and a deviation (e.g. one imposed by another agent's interfering trajectory) is detectable as a departure from rational pursuit. This grounds discriminant (2) -- whether your action obstructs the other's goal -- on a biologically-attested computation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The teleological stance is non-mentalistic by design: it computes over goals and constraints, not beliefs or consent. It therefore grounds MECH-129's first two discriminants but is silent on (3) constitutive-vs-incidental and (4) consent, which the plan correctly hands to RHM-3 and the mirror-modelling layer. It is also a review/theory paper, so the evidence is the synthesised infant literature rather than a single decisive datum.
mapping.source_context: Review of human infant (primarily 9-12 month) goal-attribution and rational-action studies

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, highly-cited TICS synthesis. Mapping fidelity good for the goal-inference rule (the bridge from goal-representation to obstruction-detection); transfer risk moderate (infant developmental theory to REE computation; non-mentalistic stance caps how far it reaches into the consent discriminant).
